key_insight: For world-action models, the representation space matters as much as the model itself: neither pixel-perfect reconstruction nor off-the-shelf perceptual features reliably produce strong robot policies. The paper shows that representation design should be calibrated for both control and prediction, leading to ReWAM.
problem_solved: The paper tackles how to choose or learn a representation space that supports both future observation prediction and effective robot policy learning in world-action models.
method: Run controlled comparisons of different representation choices to isolate what helps or hurts policy learning.
Build ReWAM, a representation-centric world-action model based on pre-trained DINO features.
Add Feature Calibration and a Temporal Representation component to better align features with action control and future prediction.
impact: This work gives practitioners a clearer principle for designing robot world models: optimize the latent space for downstream control, not just for visual fidelity. It can improve policy learning stability and performance in embodied AI systems.
